```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)

#library(patchwork)

streams <- read_excel("stream_data.xlsx")
head(streams)
```

## R Markdown


```{r models}
mod1 <- lm(links~species, data=streams)
summary(mod1)
shapiro.test(residuals(mod1))


mod2 <- lm(species~connectance, data=streams)
summary(mod2)
shapiro.test(residuals(mod2))
```

## Including Plots

```{r plot1, echo=FALSE}
a <- ggplot(streams, aes(x = species, 
                    y = links, 
                    color = region)) +
  
  geom_point(size = 3) +  
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Species and links by region",
    x = "species",
    y = "Number of link",
    color = "region") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") 

a
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

```{r}
# Create the plot with linear models for both regions on the same plot
# Create the plot with linear models for both regions on the same plot
# Fit an inverse model for each region
  model_results <- streams %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  do(model = nls(species ~ a / connectance + b, data = ., start = list(a = 1, b = 1)))

# Generate predicted values for plotting
predicted_data <- streams %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  do({
    model <- nls(connectance ~ a / species + b, data = ., start = list(a = 1, b = 0))
    data.frame(species = seq(min(.$species), max(.$species), length.out = 100),
               connectance = predict(model, newdata = data.frame(species = seq(min(.$species), max(.$species), length.out = 100))),
               region = unique(.$region))
  })

# Plot the data and fitted curves
b <- ggplot(streams, aes(x = species, y = connectance, color = region)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +  # Data points
  geom_line(data = predicted_data, aes(x = species, y = connectance, color = region), size = 1) +  # Fitted inverse lines
  labs(
    x = "Number of Species",
    y = "Connectance",
    color = "Region",
    title = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

b

```


```{r}
# Connectance by stream order s
ggplot(streams, aes(x = species, 
                    y = links, 
                    color = order)) +
  
  geom_point(size = 3) +  
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Connectance by Order",
    x = "Connectance",
    y = "Number of Species",
    color = "order") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") 
```
```{r}
# region vs species count 
# Show the number of species across different regions. This could reveal biodiversity levels in each region and help you compare species richness.
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(streams, aes(x = region, fill = order)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Species Count by Region and Order",
       x = "Region", y = "Species Count") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
ggplot(streams, aes(x = region, y = connectance, fill = order)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Connectance by Region and Order",
       x = "Region", y = "Link Density") +
  theme_minimal()


```
```{r}
#  Compare connectance across regions. This metric can give insights into ecosystem stability, as more connected networks are often more resilient.
ggplot(streams, aes(x = region, y = connectance)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(title = "Connectance by Region",
       x = "Region", y = "Connectance") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
data_summary <- streams %>%
  group_by(region, order) %>%
  summarise(species_count = sum(species))

ggplot(data_summary, aes(x = region, y = order, fill = species_count)) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(title = "Species Richness by Region and Order",
       x = "Region", y = "Order", fill = "Species Count") +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# Show correlations between numeric variables like species, links, link_density, and connectance to identify any strong relationships.
numeric_data <- streams %>% select(species, links, link_density, connectance)
ggpairs(numeric_data, title = "Correlation Matrix of Ecosystem Variables")
```
